content.figure_title: Diagnostic algorithm for patients with suspected high-risk pulmonary embolism presenting with haemodynamic instability
flow_summary: Suspected PE in a patient with haemodynamic instability -> Bedside TTE (transthoracic echocardiogram).
If no RV dysfunction on bedside TTE -> Search for other causes of shock or instability.
If RV dysfunction present -> Is CTPA (computed tomography pulmonary angiography) immediately available and feasible?
If CTPA is immediately available and feasible -> perform CTPA.
If CTPA positive -> Treatment of high-risk PE.
If CTPA negative -> Search for other causes of shock or instability.
If CTPA not immediately available/feasible -> Treatment of high-risk PE (based on echocardiographic findings and clinical situation).
content.ancillary_tests_note: Ancillary bedside imaging tests may include TOE (transoesophageal echocardiography), which may detect emboli in the pulmonary artery and its main branches; and bilateral venous CUS (compression ultrasonography), which may confirm DVT and thus VTE.
content.key_echo_definition: In the emergency situation of suspected high-risk PE, RV dysfunction refers mainly to a RV/LV diameter ratio >1.0; the echocardiographic findings of RV dysfunction and corresponding cut-off levels are presented elsewhere in the guideline.

footnotes.a: See Table 4 for definition of haemodynamic instability and high-risk PE.
footnotes.b: Ancillary bedside imaging tests may include TOE, which may detect emboli in the pulmonary artery and its main branches; and bilateral venous CUS, which may confirm DVT and thus VTE.
footnotes.c: In the emergency situation of suspected high-risk PE, this refers mainly to a RV/LV diameter ratio >1.0; echocardiographic findings of RV dysfunction and corresponding cut-off levels are graphically presented in Figure 3, and their prognostic value summarized in Supplementary Data Table 3.
footnotes.d: Includes cases in which the patient's condition is so critical that it only allows bedside diagnostic tests. In such cases, echocardiographic findings of RV dysfunction confirm high-risk PE and emergency reperfusion therapy is recommended.

content.clinical_implication: For haemodynamically unstable patients with suspected high-risk PE, bedside echocardiography (TTE/TOE) is used to identify RV dysfunction. If CTPA is immediately available it is preferred for diagnosis; if not feasible, treatment of presumed high-risk PE should be initiated based on echocardiographic findings and clinical status.
